Exploring Australia v Pakistan ODI scoring with AusPak

Who this is for

AusPak is for a cricket analyst or fan who wants to compare how Australia and Pakistan score runs and lose wickets across an ODI innings. The app helps answer one question: in which part of an innings does each side score fastest and lose wickets, and has that changed over time?

Install 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-somya090997")

Launch the app 

library(AusPak)
run_app()

The app opens in a window or in your browser. Press the stop button in the R console when you want to close it.

What The Control Does?

Control What it does
Innings Batting first (1st innings) or chasing (2nd innings)
Measure Average runs per over, or average wickets lost per over
Show by Three phases of the innings, or every individual over
Years Keeps only matches that started in this range

The two coloured boxes show how many matches each team contributes to the current view. Gold is Australia and green is Pakistan throughout the app. The section “What do the phases mean?” in the sidebar defines the phases: powerplay is overs 1 to 10, middle is overs 11 to 40, and death is overs 41 onwards.

How To Read the Results?

  1. Start with the sentence under “What stands out”. It names the phase with the biggest gap between the teams for the current settings.
  2. Compare the gold and green bars within each phase. A taller bar means faster scoring, or more wickets if you chose that measure.
  3. Check the match counts under each bar. A gap that rests on a handful of matches is weak evidence.
  4. Change the years and see whether the gap holds in other eras.

For example, with Australia batting first across all years, the app shows Australia scoring faster than Pakistan in the death overs. Narrowing the years shows how much that gap depends on which matches are included.

If the chosen settings leave fewer than three matches for either team, the app shows an amber message in place of the chart. Widen the years or switch innings to continue.

Use the function directly

The same summary the app uses is available as phase_summary():

library(AusPak)

phase_summary(aus_pak_overs, innings = 2, years = c(2010, 2020))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   batting_team phase            matches runs_per_over wickets_per_over
#>   <chr>        <fct>              <int>         <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1 Australia    Powerplay (1-10)       9          5.16           0.122 
#> 2 Australia    Middle (11-40)         9          5.06           0.0871
#> 3 Australia    Death (41+)            8          6.59           0.131 
#> 4 Pakistan     Powerplay (1-10)      15          4.58           0.127 
#> 5 Pakistan     Middle (11-40)        15          4.94           0.167 
#> 6 Pakistan     Death (41+)           12          5.89           0.443

Read the matches column alongside the averages. Late overs come from fewer matches because innings end early.

head(phase_summary(aus_pak_overs, by = "over"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   batting_team  over matches runs_per_over wickets_per_over
#>   <chr>        <dbl>   <int>         <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1 Australia        1      31          4.06           0.194 
#> 2 Australia        2      31          4.52           0.0645
#> 3 Australia        3      31          4.58           0.0645
#> 4 Australia        4      31          5.26           0.0323
#> 5 Australia        5      31          5.58           0.129 
#> 6 Australia        6      31          5.97           0.129

Limitations

  • There are 45 Australia v Pakistan ODIs in the data, so narrow year ranges leave few matches.
  • Phases are defined by over number only. Playing conditions have changed over the years, and rain-shortened matches are still grouped by over number.
  • Wickets include every dismissal type, including run-outs.
  • The app does not account for opponents’ form, pitches or conditions.

Data: ball-by-ball records from Cricsheet, accessed through the cricketdata package.
